headline: Pop-ups began as a fix for an upset advertiser

portrait.alt: Ethan Zuckerman smiling outdoors, with long hair, glasses and a blue floral shirt
portrait.credit: Ethan Zuckerman, 2019. Joi Ito. CC BY 2.0.

slides.label: The bright idea
slides.title: Free pages, paid by ads
slides.text: A carmaker complained when its banner ran on a Tripod member's page about sex. **Ethan Zuckerman's fix: open the ad in its own window.**
slides.alt: Spring Street in Williamstown, Massachusetts: brick storefronts, parked cars and a leafy tree on a sunny day
slides.credit: Spring Street, Williamstown, Massachusetts, 2010. John Phelan. CC BY 3.0.

slides.label: It worked
slides.title: A window of its own
slides.text: The ad sat beside the page, not on it, and others copied the trick. **Advertisers bought 11.3 billion pop-ups from January to July 2002**, Nielsen//NetRatings counted.
slides.alt: Gray About page of Netscape Navigator 2.02, the first browser to run JavaScript, with the Netscape N logo
slides.credit: Netscape Navigator 2.02, screenshot by Indolering, 2015. CC0.

slides.label: The backfire
slides.title: Everyone shut the window
slides.statLabel: of 2,667 web users called pop-ups very annoying (GartnerG2, 2002)
slides.text: Browser makers built in an off switch. **Phoenix, later Firefox, blocked pop-ups from its first release in 2002.** Netscape and Safari followed within months.

slides.label: Could anyone have seen it coming?
slides.title: Partly
slides.text: In a 1999 survey, 69% of users found pop-ups annoying. **A web where every site used them was harder to see.**

slides.label: The long cleanup
slides.title: Still closing windows
slides.text: Internet Explorer blocked pop-ups by default from 2004. **In 2018 Chrome began stripping ads from sites that break ad standards**, pop-ups included.

slides.label: The ledger
slides.title: Worth it?
gains: Ads sold on members' pages without setting a brand beside the content (Zuckerman, 2014)
Free homepages; about 15 million people a day viewed Tripod pages by 1999 (Zuckerman)
11.3 billion pop-up impressions bought, January to July 2002 (Nielsen//NetRatings)
costs: 78% of internet users surveyed called pop-ups very annoying, 2002 (GartnerG2)
Pop-up blocking built into Firefox, Netscape, Safari and Internet Explorer by 2004
$21.8 billion in ad revenue blocked worldwide in 2015 by ad blockers of every kind, one estimate (PageFair and Adobe)
slides.text: It solved one advertiser's problem. **It handed the cost to every reader on the web.**

slides.label: Pattern
slides.title: Great for one, bad for all
slides.text: One pop-up gets noticed. When thousands of sites use them, readers switch them off, **and browsers switch them off for everyone.**

slides.label: Lesson
slides.title: What we take from it
slides.text: A trick that works for one company can fail once everyone copies it. **Attention is shared by every site that asks for it.**
